_comment: Declarations reclassify a fidelity finding. A declaration may ONLY claim STORAGE-TRANSLATION or DELIBERATE — the loader exits with EXIT_USAGE on any other verdict, so a divergence can never declare itself a defect away. Every declaration must carry a named `fact` and a `cites` file; one without both is refused.

declarations.subject: column:id
declarations.fact: The divergence is in the SAFE direction, so it is headroom and not infidelity. `dialogFilter` declares `id:int` in the TL — a signed 32-bit wire value — while the shipped column is BIGINT, so the column is WIDER than the wire, never narrower. The C3 rule as written fires on a width mismatch in either direction and its remedy text ('a 32-bit column is a truncation, not a translation') describes the NARROW direction only. A 64-bit column cannot truncate a 32-bit value, so no Telegram id is altered by this divergence. Widening was deliberate and is required: `id` is the second column of the composite PRIMARY KEY (account_id, id) and is the PARENT leg of six declared constraints, because the child tables in this family declare `$table->bigInteger('id')`. MEASURED on MySQL 8.4.11 by direct probe against the shipped dial: `ALTER TABLE tf_dialog_filters MODIFY id INT NOT NULL` raises errno 3780, SQLSTATE HY000, 'Referencing column id and referenced column id in foreign key constraint tf_dialog_filters_color_df_widen_fk are incompatible' — and `SET SESSION foreign_key_checks = 0` does NOT bypass it (same 3780, measured). Every table in the eight-table family is simultaneously a child and, except the leaf, a parent, so no ordering avoids dropping the seven constraints first. Narrowing is therefore not merely undesirable, it is unreachable without tearing the family's constraints down and rebuilding them. SQLite cannot judge this column at all: its grammar maps both typeInteger() and typeBigInteger() to 'integer' (SQLiteGrammar.php:774,785), which is why a SQLite run reports COPYING-GAP=0 and only the MySQL engine surfaces the row. This declaration does not excuse a truncation anywhere else — it covers exactly one subject, `column:id` on one table.

declarations.subject: fk:tf_store_media->tf_store_buckets
declarations.fact: These three tables are Teleframe's OWN local storage vault, not a Telegram mirror, so there is no TL type for the audit to read. `tf_store_buckets` declares `bucket` VARCHAR(255), `kind` VARCHAR(16) (the literal comment `// store|data|backup` is the enum), `channel_id` BIGINT, `access_hash` BIGINT and `created_at_unix` INT (migration `src/Laravel/Migrations/2026_09_20_000100_create_tf_store_tables.php`:23-31). MEASURED negative: `grep -niE 'bucket|vault|backup'` returns ZERO hits across all seven TL sources (`schema/sources/TL_telegram_v227.tl`, `schema/sources/TL_mtproto_v1.tl`, `schema/sources/TL_secret.tl`, `src/Schema/schema/sources/api.tl`, `src/Schema/schema/sources/mtproto.tl`, `src/Schema/schema/sources/api_full.tl`, `src/Schema/schema/sources/mtproto_full.tl`) - exit status 1, measured. The only `storage` hits are the leaf media-format enum `storage.FileType` (`src/Schema/schema/sources/api_full.tl`:77-86), a value type with no fields of its own, referenced only as a format tag by `upload.file#96a18d5` (:495) and `upload.webFile#21e753bc` (:1005); `inputFileLocation#dfdaabe1` (:62) carries `volume_id`/`local_id`/`secret` and no `channel_id`/`access_hash`; and `grep -nE '\bkind:'` returns ZERO hits across all seven sources, so the `store|data|backup` enum has no wire counterpart at all. A bucket is a named Telegram channel this project created or joined - `docs/store.md` states it verbatim ('**Bucket = channel.** A bucket is a named Telegram channel this account created or joined') - so the resource is created BY this engine and there is no upstream Telegram object the fidelity audit could read it from. The bucket concept is out of scope for TL fidelity BY DESIGN, so no catalog entry is owed and none exists. This declaration covers exactly the one edge named by its `subject` and does not excuse any other store table.

declarations.subject: fk:tf_update_routing_ack->tf_update_routing
declarations.fact: `tf_update_routing` is this engine's local delivery-receipt registry for the `Updates` CONTAINER, and the catalog deliberately mirrors the inner `Update` constructor (`tf_updates`, tl `Update`) rather than the `Updates` result, so the container's receipt table has no TL type by design. The parent stores `account_id`, `seq`, `position`, `constructor` VARCHAR(64) and `msg_id` BIGINT (`src/Laravel/Migrations/2026_09_14_200030_create_tf_updates_tables.php`:241-249). Per column, MEASURED against `src/Schema/schema/sources/api_full.tl`: `date` is a genuine container field - `updates#74ae4240 updates:Vector<Update> users:Vector<User> chats:Vector<Chat> date:int seq:int = Updates;` (:487) and `updatesCombined#725b04c3 updates:Vector<Update> users:Vector<User> chats:Vector<Chat> date:int seq_start:int seq:int = Updates;` (:486) both declare `date:int`; `seq_start` is genuine and `updatesCombined`-only, since :486 declares `seq_start:int` and :487 does not. But `msg_id` is NOT a field on any of the seven container constructors - it is the transport envelope id this engine assigns, and the migration docblock says so verbatim ("'msg_id' is the transport envelope message id (0 for non-pushed receipts) - the quick-ack registry key the wire layer reads", :29-31). Likewise `acked`/`acked_at` are the wire layer's quick-ack disposition (migration :274-281, whose comment reads "Quick-ack disposition: the wire layer flips 'acked' once msg_ack is") and are absent from every TL source: across all seven sources the only `acked` occurrences are the substring inside `gzip_packed`/`GzipPacked` (`src/Schema/schema/sources/mtproto.tl`:93, `src/Schema/schema/sources/mtproto_full.tl`:42,77, `schema/sources/TL_mtproto_v1.tl`:42,77), none of which is a field name. So this family is deliberately a mixed engine-receipt store - some legs are faithful container fields, others are transport-envelope bookkeeping - not a claim to mirror `Updates`, and the three child tables are its per-field legs. This declaration covers exactly the three edges named by these subjects.

declarations.subject: fk:tf_channel_participants->tf_channels
declarations.fact: This edge is NOT a nesting and is not claimed to be one. MEASURED: no `channelParticipant*` constructor declares `channel_id` - `schema/sources/TL_telegram_v227.tl`:766-771 are `channelParticipant#1bd54456 flags:# user_id:long date:int subscription_until_date:flags.0?int rank:flags.2?string = ChannelParticipant;`, `channelParticipantSelf#a9478a1a ...`, `channelParticipantCreator#2fe601d3 ...`, `channelParticipantAdmin#34c3bb53 ...`, `channelParticipantBanned#d5f0ad91 ...`, and `channelParticipantLeft#1b03f006 peer:Peer = ChannelParticipant;` (:771) - and the channel arrives from the ENCLOSING update instead: `updateChannelParticipant#985d3abb flags:# via_chatlist:flags.3?true channel_id:long date:int actor_id:long user_id:long prev_participant:flags.0?ChannelParticipant new_participant:flags.1?ChannelParticipant invite:flags.2?ExportedChatInvite qts:int = Update;` (:403). The catalog already models exactly that: `tf_channel_participants.sources` in `src/Schema/schema/mirror-catalog.json` declares `{"ctor":"updateChannelParticipant","field":"new_participant","context":["channel_id"]}` and the same for `prev_participant`, and `MeRezaRezaei\Teleframe\Schema\Mirror\MirrorCatalog::assertDerivable()` (`src/Schema/Mirror/MirrorCatalog.php`:157) admits a param supplied by a declared `sources` context overlay - its third derivable shape, documented in the body as the arm that lets a nested fact's key come from the ENCLOSING object rather than from the entry's own TL type. `channel_id` is therefore a canonical peer reference the update supplies, and the constraint enforces only that the referenced channel row exists. The migration states the intent verbatim: "tf_channel_participants (account_id, channel_id) -> tf_channels (account_id, id) RESTRICT - the participant's channel is a canonical peer ref; RESTRICT (not cascade) keeps a participant channel from being vanished out from under its rows" (`src/Laravel/Migrations/2026_09_14_299999_create_tf_foreign_keys.php`:41-44), with the constraint itself at :118. The audit reports an empty field name here because `childFieldName()` in `bin/audit-fidelity.php` is a pure string-prefix test - it requires the child table to be name-shaped as `<parent>_` plus a field, and `tf_channel_participants` is not shaped that way relative to `tf_channels_`. The empty name is the tool's blindness to a peer-ref edge, not a statement that the constraint is unfounded.

declarations.subject: fk:tf_updates_peer->tf_updates
declarations.fact: `tf_updates_peer` stores `peer_type` TINYINT plus `peer_id` BIGINT (`src/Laravel/Migrations/2026_09_14_200030_create_tf_updates_tables.php`:174-178) - this repo's established storage translation for a `Peer` union, and identical in shape to `tf_updates_from` on the very next block (:182-186). Every `Update` constructor that declares `peer` declares a NESTED UNION, never a scalar. MEASURED across all 160 constructors whose declaration ends `= Update;` in `schema/sources/TL_telegram_v227.tl` (`grep -cE '= Update;$'` returns 160): 36 declare a `peer` param - 30 as `peer:Peer` (`updateReadHistoryInbox` :334, `updateReadHistoryOutbox` :335, `updateBotCallbackQuery` :352, `updateDraftMessage` :356, `updateChatDefaultBannedRights` :377, `updatePeerSettings` :379, `updateMessagePollVote` :386, `updatePinnedMessages` :396, and 22 more), 3 as `peer:DialogPeer` (`updateDialogPinned` :362, `updateDialogUnreadMark` :375, `updateSavedDialogPinned` :433 - and `dialogPeer#e56dbf05 peer:Peer = DialogPeer;` :1149 is itself nested), 1 as `peer:NotifyPeer` (`updateNotifySettings` :330 - and `notifyPeer#9fd40bd8 peer:Peer = NotifyPeer;` :542 is itself nested), and 2 as conditional `peer:flags.N?Peer` (`updateMessagePoll` :376, `updateGroupCall` :400). None of these 36 declares `peer` as a scalar: the only scalar `peer:` field anywhere in the file is `inputAppEvent#1d1b1245 time:double type:string peer:long data:JSONValue` (:1234), which is an `inputAppEvent` and not an `Update`. A child table for a nested union is therefore faithful storage translation, not over-decomposition. The audit reads silent because `paramAcrossCtors()` in `bin/audit-fidelity.php` (:870) searches ONLY the 11 constructors the catalog curates for `tf_updates` - `updateNewMessage`, `updateEditMessage`, `updateNewChannelMessage`, `updateEditChannelMessage`, `updateDeleteMessages`, `updateUserStatus`, `updateUserTyping`, `updateChatUserTyping`, `updateChannelUserTyping`, `updateChannelParticipant`, `updateChannelTooLong` (all 11 verified to declare no `peer` param) - and that curated subset is a catalog scope limit, not a statement about Telegram. The table is deliberately the same shape as `tf_updates_from`, which `src/Laravel/Migrations/2026_10_10_000100_fold_update_scalar_children_onto_the_update_fact.php` explicitly refused to fold for precisely this reason (its `tf_updates` fold list marks `tf_updates_from` DELIBERATELY ABSENT, because `from_id` is `Peer` on every `Update` ctor that declares it rather than a bare `long`).

declarations.subject: fk:tf_updates_pts_count->tf_updates_pts
declarations.fact: This row is blind because the PARENT is not a Telegram object, and that is structural rather than an omission. `tf_updates_pts` is a scalar-PRESENCE child: `src/Schema/schema/mirror-catalog.json` declares `tf_updates.children` as the pair `["pts","INTEGER NOT NULL"]`, and `MeRezaRezaei\Teleframe\Schema\Mirror\MirrorTableResolver::resolveTable()` turns EVERY `children` entry into a child TABLE because row existence IS fact existence (see its own comment, 'Scalar-shaped catalog children ... must be mirrored, not dropped'). The field it stores, `Update.pts`, is a TL scalar, so `bin/audit-fidelity.php`'s `resolveProvenance()` returns no TL type for the child BY CONSTRUCTION -- there is no Telegram object at a scalar, so there is nothing for the audit to read. That is why the audit reports 'holds NO TL type', and it is the same shape as `tf_chats_access_hash`, which the audit does not raise at all because `tf_chats` IS a catalog entry. The CONSTRAINT is nonetheless true on the wire, and measured: across all 160 `Update` constructors of `schema/sources/TL_telegram_v227.tl`, 14 declare both `pts` and `pts_count` (e.g. `updateNewMessage#1f2b0afd message:Message pts:int pts_count:int = Update;`), 2 declare `pts` alone (`updateChannelTooLong`, `updateReadChannelInbox`), and ZERO declare `pts_count` without `pts`. Every pts_count row therefore implies a pts row, so the constraint refuses no valid Telegram data. It is deliberately KEPT rather than dropped, and the reason is mechanical: `MeRezaRezaei\Teleframe\Schema\Mirror\MirrorRelationPlan::reflect()` derives a child's parent by LONGEST name prefix over the executed DDL, so `tf_updates_pts_count` resolves to `tf_updates_pts` and not to `tf_updates`, and `tests/Schema/Mirror/EveryFkableRelationHasAConstraintTest.php` requires a constraint on every such derived relation. MEASURED on this tree: dropping `tf_updates_pts_count_udiff_parent_fk` makes that gate report `tf_updates_pts_count(account_id,seq,position) -> tf_updates_pts` missing. The correct sibling edge is not lost -- `tf_updates_pts_count` already carries `tf_updates_pts_count_account_id_seq_position_foreign -> tf_updates`. This covers exactly this one edge.
